explanation: Backup / tiered-storage (tierNAS) level ransomware detection -- confirmed via a real product QA test spec (2026-08-27). A dedicated backup-tier binary (documented only as '<backup binary>', exact name not given in the source spec) updates /athinio/security/tierNAS_ransomware.xml's <RansomDetected> tag to 'YES' when it detects tampering. /athinio/bin/gatewayMonitor.sh reads that file and sets /athinio/system/alertlog.xml's <tierNas_ransom> to 1, which rolls up directly to Alert.xml's tier_ran tag. The documented test case is overwriting 5 files and running scr_cron, which should then update more than 5 files inside oneCloud/Backup -- i.e. this checks tampering specifically within the backup/tiered-storage path, not the live production filesystem oneCloudFilerx watches for gateway_ransomware_filesystem.

metadata.writer_script: backup-tier binary (exact name not confirmed in source spec) -> /athinio/security/tierNAS_ransomware.xml's RansomDetected -> /athinio/bin/gatewayMonitor.sh -> athinio/system/alertlog.xml's tierNas_ransom, rolling up to Alert.xml's tier_ran
metadata.confidence: verified mechanism per a real product QA test spec, but the specific backup-tier binary name was not given in that source; tier_ran/tierNas_ransom both confirmed present and reading 0 (clean) on a real hierarchy

value_meanings.0: Clean -- no tampering detected in the backup/tiered-storage path (oneCloud/Backup) since the last reset. Confirmed live on real hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 (2026-08-27).
value_meanings.1: Backup-level ransomware detected -- files within the tiered-storage backup path were tampered with, per the documented test pattern of overwriting backup files faster than the normal backup-cron cadence accounts for.

metadata.caveat: requires_live_recompute for the same reason as gateway_ransomware_filesystem -- the underlying trigger is inside a compiled binary this workflow can't independently re-derive from a snapshot. Distinct from BOTH the plain 'ransomware' entry (production-path RefCopy/bin/lib diff) and 'gateway_ransomware_filesystem' (oneCloudFilerx's live production file-count threshold) -- this one is scoped specifically to the backup/tiered-storage copy, so a clean read here does not imply the production copies are also clean, and vice versa.
